sentences.text: The species is known from a single nearly complete skeleton, specimen CAGS-IG-04-0801, measuring 55 centimeters in length.
The specimen preserves extensive pennaceous feathers but lacks flight feathers on its hind legs.
Feather impressions are found around the neck, body, hips, upper hindlimbs, tail, and near the hands.
The dinosaur possessed long, vaned tail feathers that grew progressively longer toward the tip.
The animal featured an elongated claw on the second toe of its hind feet.
The name Jinfengopteryx derives from Jinfeng, the golden phoenix mother of all birds in Chinese mythology, and the Greek word pteryx meaning feather.
Jinfengopteryx fossils were discovered in the Qiaotou Member of the Huajiying Formation in Hebei Province, China.
Small reddish-yellow oval structures preserved in the fossil may be seeds the dinosaur ate, suggesting an omnivorous diet.
The species belongs to the subfamily Jinfengopteryginae.
The animal likely lived approximately 122 million years ago during the Early Cretaceous.
The animal lived during the early Cretaceous, approximately 143 to 128 million years ago, between the Berriasian and Hauterivian stages.
The time range for the genus is recorded as the Barremian stage, from 125.77 to 121.4 million years ago.
The diet is uncertain; despite being a theropod, it may have been a herbivore.
